text:
A: Hello. Can you hear me all right?
B: Yes, hello! I'm Marites. Sorry, my phone is on the rice cooker.
A: Neil. That's quite all right. I'm told this is genuinely the last one. I said that to someone in the previous call and I was wrong.
B: Hehe, yes, I think this is the last. My head is tired now.
A: Mine too. Lots of names. Er, what is it you do, Marites?
B: I'm a carer. Home care, in Croydon. I go to the old people's houses, washing, dressing, meals, medicine.
A: That's a demanding job. Do you see a lot of people with dementia?
B: Yes, quite a lot. Some of my clients, yes. Sorry, why, you have somebody?
A: My wife's mum. She's in the early stages. It's mostly small things at the moment, repeating herself, getting worried in the afternoons. Julie's finding it hard. I don't always know what to say to her mum when she gets anxious.
B: Oh, I'm sorry. Yes, the afternoon is always worse. We say sundowning. What I do, I don't argue with them. If she says it's Tuesday and it's Friday, okay, it's Tuesday. Then I give her something to do with her hands. Folding towels, making tea together. And I talk slowly, nice and calm. It works, mostly.
A: Don't argue. That's useful. I think I'm inclined to correct people, it's a habit from work.
B: Hehe, yes, everybody does that first. But she will just feel bad, and then more worried. Better she feels safe. Also old photos, they like the old photos. They remember those ones better than yesterday.
A: That's very kind of you to explain. Thank you. I'll pass that on to Julie.
B: You're welcome. What do you do, Neil? You look like a teacher, sorry.
A: I've had that before. No, I manage the maintenance and health and safety at a factory in Loughborough. Packaging.
B: Oh, a boss.
A: A sort of boss. A boss who fixes things, mostly. Do you enjoy your work?
B: Yes. I like the people. Only the buses I don't like. Sometimes I spend more time on the bus than with the clients.
A: That sounds very inefficient. Is there no way of getting them closer together?
B: I asked before. The coordinator says she will try. She always says that, hehe.
A: It's worth asking again, I think. They'd lose a lot if they lost you, by the sound of it.
B: Oh, thank you. I don't like to ask too much.
A: Well. Can I ask, are you from the Philippines originally?
B: Yes, Pampanga. North of Manila. You know it?
A: Only the name, I'm afraid. I've never been further east than Krakow.
B: Krakow, Poland? Tomasz is from Poland!
A: He is. He gave me instructions for fixing my bike. This study is turning out to be quite practical.
B: Hehe. Yes, Rob told me about going back to study, and you told me about, erm
